title: Qlik Sense alternatives (2026): 8 BI tools compared for teams leaving QlikView or Qlik Cloud capacity pricing
summary: Power BI, Tableau, Sigma, ThoughtSpot, Omni, Metabase, Astrato, and Basedash compared as Qlik alternatives on pricing, live queries, RLS, SSO, and AI.
body_markdown:
The strongest Qlik Sense alternatives in 2026 are Power BI and Tableau for enterprises that want another established suite, Sigma, Omni, and Astrato for teams moving to live queries on a cloud warehouse, ThoughtSpot for search-style AI analytics, Metabase for a low-cost or open-source option, and Basedash for small teams that want AI chat on top of their database. The right pick depends on why you are leaving Qlik: an aging QlikView estate, Qlik Cloud’s data-capacity pricing, or the in-memory reload model. Every price and plan below was checked on the vendor’s official page on September 27, 2026.


## Why teams look for a Qlik alternative in 2026


Qlik is still a capable platform. Its associative engine, set analysis, and load scripting are powerful once a team has learned them, and Gartner has named Qlik a leader in its analytics and BI Magic Quadrant for 16 straight years, according to[Qlik’s trial page](https://www.qlik.com/us/trial/qlik-sense-business) . Teams usually start shopping for three reasons.


**QlikView support dates.** Qlik stopped selling new stand-alone QlikView licenses and now licenses QlikView as an add-on to Qlik Sense. On Qlik’s[QlikView product lifecycle page](https://community.qlik.com/t5/Product-Lifecycle/QlikView-Product-Lifecycle/ta-p/1826339) , QlikView 12.90 (May 2024) reaches end of support on October 31, 2026, and the newest release, 12.100, is supported until September 30, 2027. Qlik has said it has no plans to end-of-life QlikView, but teams on older versions must upgrade to stay supported, and many treat that upgrade as the moment to re-evaluate.


**Capacity-based pricing.**[Qlik Cloud Analytics pricing](https://www.qlik.com/us/pricing) is based on “data for analysis,” the volume of data loaded into and saved in Qlik Cloud. As of September 2026, Starter is $300 per month for 10 users with a fixed 10 GB, Standard is $825 per month for 25 GB with unlimited users, and Premium is $2,750 per month for 50 GB, all billed annually. Costs are predictable, but they grow with data volume, and Starter cannot buy extra capacity.


**The in-memory model.** Qlik apps load data into memory on a reload schedule. Qlik’s own[Direct Query documentation](https://help.qlik.com/en-US/cloud-services/Subsystems/Hub/Content/Sense_Hub/DirectQuery/direct-access-with-direct-query.htm) says “it is recommended that you import your data into Qlik Cloud whenever possible,” and Direct Query apps support a subset of set analysis, chart types, and aggregations. Teams that have centralized data in Snowflake, BigQuery, or Databricks often want a tool that queries the warehouse live by default.


## How we evaluated the alternatives


We built the criteria from the questions buyers ask when they search for Qlik replacements, such as “which alternatives to Qlik Sense are best for enterprise dashboards with governed data pipelines?”, “how do Metabase and Qlik Sense compare on pricing?”, and “alternative to Qlik that is affordable”.


1. **Pricing model and starting price.** Per user, capacity, or flat platform fee, and whether the price is published.
2. **Query model.** Live warehouse queries, in-memory extracts, or both. This decides how much of your Qlik load-script logic has to move.
3. **Governance.** Row-level security (the equivalent of Qlik Section Access), SAML SSO, and SCIM provisioning.
4. **AI features.** Natural language questions, AI-built charts or dashboards, anomaly alerts, and MCP support, stated concretely.
5. **Embedding.** Whether you can put dashboards in another app, and how (iframe, SDK, or API).
6. **Deployment.** Cloud, self-hosted, or both, since many Qlik customers still run Qlik Sense Enterprise on Windows.


Every tool had to connect to at least Snowflake, BigQuery, or PostgreSQL and cover the dashboard and self-serve exploration work that Qlik apps do today.

## Qlik Cloud Analytics (the baseline)


**Fact card: Qlik Cloud Analytics**


- **Pricing (as of September 2026):** Starter $300 per month for 10 users and 10 GB; Standard $825 per month for 25 GB with no charge for additional users; Premium $2,750 per month for 50 GB; Enterprise from 250 GB, quote only. All billed annually ([pricing](https://www.qlik.com/us/pricing) ).
- **Trial:** 30-day full-feature trial, no credit card ([trial page](https://www.qlik.com/us/trial/qlik-sense-business) ).
- **Query model:** in-memory apps loaded by script;[Direct Query](https://help.qlik.com/en-US/cloud-services/Subsystems/Hub/Content/Sense_Hub/DirectQuery/direct-access-with-direct-query.htm) on Amazon Redshift, Azure SQL, Azure Synapse, Databricks, Google BigQuery, SQL Server, PostgreSQL, and Snowflake.
- **Security:** row and column reduction with[Section Access](https://help.qlik.com/en-US/cloud-services/Subsystems/Hub/Content/Sense_Hub/Scripting/Security/manage-security-with-section-access.htm) ; SAML or OIDC identity providers;[SCIM 2.0 provisioning](https://help.qlik.com/en-US/cloud-services/Subsystems/Hub/Content/Sense_Hub/Admin/auto-provisioning-using-SCIM.htm) with Microsoft Entra ID only.
- **AI features:** Qlik Answers agents and an MCP server on every Cloud plan; AutoML predictive analytics on Premium.
- **Embedding:**[qlik-embed](https://qlik.dev/embed/) web components and APIs; anonymous public access on Premium and above.


Knowing this baseline matters because migrations fail when a team replaces Qlik without a plan for its load scripts and Section Access tables. Those two pieces hold most of the business logic in a mature Qlik estate.


## Power BI


**Best for:** Microsoft 365 organizations that want the lowest per-user price among the established suites.


Power BI is the most common destination for Qlik customers, largely because many already pay for Microsoft 365 E5, which includes Power BI Pro. Power Query and DAX replace Qlik’s load script and set analysis, and the skills map reasonably well.


**Fact card: Power BI**


- **Pricing (as of September 2026):** Free account; Pro $14 per user per month; Premium Per User $24; Embedded and Fabric capacity priced separately ([pricing](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/products/power-bi/pricing) ).
- **Query model:** import (8 refreshes per day on Pro, 48 on PPU) or DirectQuery.
- **Security:**[row-level security](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/security/service-admin-row-level-security) with roles and DAX filters, applied to Viewer users; identity through Microsoft Entra ID.
- **AI features:** Copilot for report building, summaries, and DAX, which requires a paid Fabric capacity (F2 or higher) or Premium P1; Pro or PPU alone is not enough ([Copilot requirements](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/copilot-introduction) ).
- **Embedding:** Power BI Embedded, with viewer access without per-user licenses on F64 or P1 and above.
- **Not ideal for:** Mac-only teams (Power BI Desktop runs on Windows) or teams that want AI chat without buying Fabric capacity.


**Tradeoffs:** Power BI is cheap per seat, but the total cost moves to Fabric capacity once you want Copilot, large models, or license-free viewers. DAX has a learning curve similar to Qlik set analysis.


## Tableau


**Best for:** analyst teams that care most about visual exploration and want both a cloud and a self-managed option.


Tableau is the other enterprise suite Qlik customers compare against. It connects live or through extracts, so teams can keep Qlik-style in-memory performance where they need it and query the warehouse live elsewhere.


**Fact card: Tableau**


- **Pricing (as of September 2026):** Standard from $15 per user per month and Enterprise from $35, billed annually; Tableau Cloud+ contact sales; Tableau Next from $40. Every deployment needs at least one Creator license and all plans are annual ([pricing](https://www.tableau.com/pricing) ).
- **Free option:** Tableau Desktop Free Edition for local analysis, without publishing.
- **Deployment:** Tableau Cloud or self-managed Tableau Server.
- **Security:** user filters and entitlement tables for row-level security; SAML SSO;[SCIM on Tableau Cloud](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/scim_config_online.htm) .
- **AI features:** Tableau Pulse metrics on Standard; Tableau Agent in Tableau Cloud and Pulse on Cloud+.
- **Not ideal for:** teams that want monthly billing or AI chat without the premium edition.


**Tradeoffs:** Tableau’s authoring is strong, but its role-based license mix (Creator, Explorer, Viewer) needs planning to avoid overbuying. Qlik’s associative filtering has no exact equivalent, so rebuilt dashboards often need redesigned interactions.


## Sigma


**Best for:** finance and operations teams moving from Qlik to Snowflake or Databricks who want a spreadsheet interface on live warehouse data.


Sigma stores no copy of your data. Every workbook queries the warehouse, which removes the reload scripts that Qlik apps depend on.


**Fact card: Sigma**


- **Pricing (as of September 2026):** quote only; the pricing page routes to a sales form ([sigmacomputing.com/pricing](https://www.sigmacomputing.com/pricing) ). Free trial available.
- **Databases:** Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift, PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, and others.
- **Query model:** live warehouse queries with caching; no extracts.
- **Security:**[row-level security](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/set-up-row-level-security) through user attributes; SAML 2.0;[SCIM](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/manage-users-and-teams-with-scim) .
- **AI features:** Sigma Assistant for natural language questions, plus an MCP server.
- **Embedding:** secure embeds signed with JWT, and public embeds.
- **Not ideal for:** teams without a cloud warehouse, or buyers who want a public price.


**Tradeoffs:** Sigma is only as fast as your warehouse, and warehouse compute becomes part of the BI bill. Teams used to Qlik’s in-memory speed should load-test large workbooks during a trial.


## ThoughtSpot


**Best for:** organizations that want business users to search and chat with governed data instead of navigating dashboards.


ThoughtSpot is the tool buyers most often compare with Qlik on conversational analytics. It is built around search, and its Spotter agent answers natural language questions on live warehouse data.


**Fact card: ThoughtSpot**


- **Pricing (as of September 2026):** $25 per user per month for 5 to 50 users and 25 million rows; Pro $50 per user per month with Spotter (25 queries per user per month) for up to 1,000 users and 250 million rows; Enterprise custom; credit-based option from $0.10 per credit ([pricing](https://www.thoughtspot.com/pricing) ).
- **Trial:** 14-day free trial.
- **Query model:** live connections to Snowflake, Databricks, Redshift, and others; Spotcache in-memory cache is an add-on.
- **Security:** row-level security, SAML, OAuth, and OIDC.
- **AI features:** Spotter agents, automated KPI monitoring with anomaly detection and alerts; the MCP server is an add-on.
- **Embedding:** ThoughtSpot Embedded with REST API and SDK, priced separately.
- **Not ideal for:** teams that need pixel-controlled, report-style dashboards.


**Tradeoffs:** ThoughtSpot needs a clean, well-modeled data layer for search to work. Row limits on the lower tiers matter for Qlik customers with large apps.


## Omni


**Best for:** data teams that want a governed semantic model, similar to what a mature Qlik estate encodes in load scripts, without LookML.


Omni combines a semantic layer with spreadsheet, SQL, and point-and-click analysis on the same model, and queries the warehouse live.


**Fact card: Omni**


- **Pricing (as of September 2026):** quote only; Omni does not publish a pricing page.
- **Databases:** Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift, PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, Trino, MySQL, MotherDuck, and SQL Server.
- **Query model:** live queries with a configurable query cache (6 hours by default).
- **Security:** access filters on user attributes for row-level security; SAML or OIDC; SCIM for Okta, Entra ID, and Rippling ([docs](https://docs.omni.co/) ).
- **AI features:** AI chat grounded in the semantic model, and an MCP server.
- **Embedding:** SSO embedding, plus an AI chat API for embedded use.
- **Not ideal for:** teams that want self-hosting or published prices.


**Tradeoffs:** Omni rewards teams that invest in modeling. A small team that only needs a few dashboards may find the modeling layer more than it needs.


## Metabase


**Best for:** small and midsize teams that want the cheapest path off Qlik, with an open-source option to self-host.


Buyers ask directly how Metabase and Qlik Sense compare on pricing. The short answer: Metabase open source is free, and Metabase Cloud Starter costs about a third of Qlik Cloud Starter for a smaller team.


**Fact card: Metabase**


- **Pricing (as of September 2026):** Open Source free; Starter $100 per month ($90 billed yearly) for 5 users; Pro from $575 per month, then $12 per user per month after 5 users; Enterprise from $20,000 per year. Metabase AI costs $3.75 per million tokens, or you can bring your own key. Embedded users count as users ([pricing](https://www.metabase.com/pricing) ).
- **Deployment:** Metabase Cloud or self-hosted.
- **Query model:** live queries against 20+ supported databases.
- **Security:** row and column permissions, SSO, and[SCIM](https://www.metabase.com/docs/latest/people-and-groups/user-provisioning) on Pro and Enterprise.
- **AI features:** Metabot natural language questions and SQL generation, including in open source.
- **Embedding:** guest embeds on all plans; the[embedded analytics SDK](https://www.metabase.com/docs/latest/embedding/sdk/introduction) for React and multi-tenant embedding on Pro.
- **Not ideal for:** enterprises that need Qlik-level governance and complex calculated models.


**Tradeoffs:** Metabase is easy to start, but row-level security and SSO require Pro, which moves a 25-user team to roughly $815 per month. Complex Qlik expressions usually have to be rewritten as SQL models.


## Astrato


**Best for:** Qlik and Tableau customers modernizing to a warehouse-native setup who want vendor-led migration help.


Astrato explicitly markets “Qlik / Tableau modernisation” on its pricing page and offers dashboard migration and parallel-run rollouts.


**Fact card: Astrato**


- **Pricing (as of September 2026):** quote only across Team, Platform, and Embedded plans, priced on adoption and concurrency rather than seats. Astrato says it will honor your current BI licensing term during migration ([pricing](https://astrato.io/pricing) ).
- **Databases:** Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift, PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, and Dremio.
- **Query model:** live pushdown SQL with no extracts.
- **Security:** inherits warehouse row-level security or uses roles defined in Astrato; OAuth on Team; SAML, LDAP, and SCIM on Platform.
- **AI features:** AI dashboard builder on Team; GenAI integration with Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, and Snowflake Cortex on Platform.
- **Embedding:** iframe embeds with JWT or SSO pass-through; multi-tenant and white-label on Embedded.
- **Not ideal for:** teams that want a self-serve trial and public pricing, or that do not have a cloud warehouse.


**Tradeoffs:** Astrato is smaller than the other vendors here, so check its roadmap and support coverage during evaluation. Writeback is a strength for teams that used Qlik extensions for planning workflows.


## Basedash


**Best for:** small and midsize teams that want business users to ask questions in plain English against a live database instead of rebuilding Qlik apps one by one.


Basedash is an AI-native BI tool. Users describe what they want, the[AI data analyst](https://www.basedash.com/features/ai-data-analyst) writes and runs the SQL, and results save to[dashboards](https://www.basedash.com/features/dashboards) as editable charts. There is no load script to port.


**Fact card: Basedash**


- **Pricing (as of September 2026):** Startup $1,000 per month plus AI usage, for up to 25 users, with $1,000 per month in AI credits included; Enterprise custom ([pricing](https://www.basedash.com/pricing) ). 14-day free trial, no card required.
- **Deployment:** cloud;[self-hosting](https://www.basedash.com/features/self-hosting) on Enterprise.
- **Databases:** live queries on PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, and other databases, plus 750+ SaaS sources synced into the managed[Basedash Warehouse](https://www.basedash.com/features/warehouse) .
- **Security:**[row-level security](https://www.basedash.com/docs/features/row-level-security) through PostgreSQL policies keyed on the` basedash.groups` session variable; other databases rely on their own access controls plus Basedash data source permissions. SAML and OIDC SSO,[SCIM](https://www.basedash.com/features/scim) , and audit logs are on Enterprise.
- **AI features:** chat analysis, AI-generated dashboards, daily anomaly detection with[Insights](https://www.basedash.com/features/insights) , and an[MCP server](https://www.basedash.com/features/mcp-server) on every plan.
- **Embedding:** white-labeled[embedding](https://www.basedash.com/features/embedding) on Enterprise.
- **Not ideal for:** enterprises that need per-user row filtering on Snowflake or BigQuery inside the BI layer, SSO on the Startup plan, or pixel-perfect report layouts.


**Tradeoffs:** Basedash’s flat price is simple to budget up to 25 users, but a three-person team pays less with Metabase or Power BI. It suits teams replacing Qlik’s day-to-day questions and dashboards, not a heavily governed enterprise Qlik estate.


## Other options: Domo and Looker


Domo also competes for Qlik customers, but Progress Software closed its acquisition of Domo in September 2026, so check the roadmap before committing. See[what the Domo acquisition means and its alternatives](https://www.basedash.com/blog/domo-acquired-by-progress-software-alternatives) . Looker suits teams that want LookML governance on Google Cloud; the[Looker alternatives comparison](https://www.basedash.com/vs/looker-alternatives) covers its tradeoffs.


## Which Qlik alternative should you choose?


- **You run on Microsoft 365 and want the lowest seat price:** Power BI. Budget for Fabric capacity if you want Copilot.
- **You need self-managed deployment, like Qlik Sense Enterprise on Windows:** Tableau Server, or self-hosted Metabase for smaller teams.
- **Your data already lives in Snowflake, BigQuery, or Databricks and you want to stop reloading apps:** Sigma, Omni, or Astrato.
- **You want governed dashboards with a semantic model and data pipelines behind them:** Omni or Tableau Enterprise, with Astrato if you want migration help.
- **You want business users to chat with data instead of browsing dashboards:** ThoughtSpot for enterprises, Basedash for small and midsize teams.
- **You need an affordable replacement for fewer than 10 users:** Metabase open source or Starter.
- **You need embedded analytics in your own product:** ThoughtSpot Embedded, Sigma, Metabase Pro, or Astrato Embedded. The[embedded analytics platforms comparison](https://www.basedash.com/blog/best-embedded-analytics-platforms-compared-2026) goes deeper.


For a side-by-side of how these tools gate SSO, SCIM, and RLS by plan, see[BI tool security features by plan](https://www.basedash.com/blog/bi-tool-security-features-by-plan-sso-scim-rls-audit-logs-2026) .


## How to plan a migration off Qlik


1. **Inventory apps by usage.** Most Qlik estates have a long tail of apps nobody opens. Migrate the apps people actually use.
2. **Move load-script logic upstream.** Rebuild transformations in your warehouse or dbt so the new BI tool reads clean tables instead of re-creating Qlik scripts.
3. **Translate Section Access.** Map each Section Access table to the new tool’s row-level security model, and test with real user accounts before cutover.
4. **Run in parallel.** Keep Qlik read-only for a reporting cycle and compare numbers on your top dashboards.
5. **Time the contract.** Qlik Cloud plans are billed annually, so plan the cutover before renewal.


## Frequently asked questions


### Which alternatives to Qlik Sense are best for enterprise dashboards with governed data pipelines?


Tableau Enterprise, Omni, and Power BI with Fabric are the strongest fits. Tableau Enterprise adds data management and data policies on top of live or extract connections. Omni puts a semantic model between the warehouse and every dashboard, so metric definitions are shared. Power BI pairs semantic models with Fabric pipelines. In all three, move transformation logic out of the BI layer and into the warehouse or dbt, so pipelines are governed once instead of inside each Qlik-style load script.


### How do Metabase and Qlik Sense compare on pricing?


As of September 2026, Qlik Cloud Analytics Starter costs $300 per month for 10 users and a fixed 10 GB of data, billed annually, and Standard costs $825 per month for 25 GB with unlimited users. Metabase open source is free to self-host, Metabase Cloud Starter costs $100 per month for 5 users, and Pro starts at $575 per month plus $12 per user after 5. Qlik charges by data volume; Metabase charges by user.


### Is QlikView end of life?


No. Qlik stopped selling new stand-alone QlikView licenses, but it still releases updates and has said it has no plans to end-of-life the product. Individual versions do lose support: QlikView 12.90 (May 2024) reaches end of support on October 31, 2026, and 12.100 is supported until September 30, 2027. Unsupported versions keep running, but Qlik will not support them until you upgrade.


### Is Qlik similar to Power BI?


Both are established BI suites with in-memory engines, scripted data preparation, and governed sharing, so they solve similar problems. They differ in pricing and ecosystem. Qlik Cloud charges by data capacity, starting at $300 per month. Power BI charges per user, with Pro at $14 per month, and pushes larger workloads and Copilot onto Fabric capacity. Power BI fits Microsoft 365 organizations; Qlik’s associative filtering has no direct Power BI equivalent.


### What is an affordable Qlik alternative for a small team?


For under 10 users, Metabase is the cheapest option: open source is free, and Metabase Cloud Starter is $100 per month for 5 users. Power BI Pro at $14 per user per month is affordable if your team already uses Microsoft 365. Basedash’s Startup plan is $1,000 per month for up to 25 users with AI credits included, which fits teams that want AI chat rather than the lowest price.


### Which Qlik alternatives work for embedded analytics?


ThoughtSpot Embedded offers a REST API and SDK with multi-tenant support. Sigma supports JWT-signed secure embeds. Metabase offers guest embeds on every plan and a React SDK with multi-tenant data segregation on Pro. Astrato’s Embedded plan adds white-labeling and usage-based scaling, and Basedash offers white-labeled embedding on Enterprise. Check whether each vendor counts embedded viewers as billable users; Metabase does.


### How does ThoughtSpot compare to Qlik for AI analytics?


ThoughtSpot is built around search and its Spotter AI agents, which answer natural language questions on live warehouse data; the Pro plan includes 25 Spotter queries per user per month at $50 per user. Qlik Cloud includes Qlik Answers agents and an MCP server on every plan, but most Qlik apps still run on in-memory data loaded by script. Teams that want search-first analytics on a warehouse lean toward ThoughtSpot.
